claims.text: Wear resistance of an HEA coating on a transition-metal matrix initially improves as ambient temperature rises.
The improvement in wear resistance persists up to a critical temperature of approximately 600–700 K.
Thermally activated formation of a protective, self-healing oxide scale causes the initial improvement in wear resistance.
Wear resistance degrades rapidly above the critical temperature.
A transition from dislocation glide to diffusion-controlled creep contributes to high-temperature wear degradation.
Destabilization of coherent nanoprecipitates contributes to high-temperature wear degradation.
W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr and AlCoCrFeNi are candidate refractory HEA coating systems for deposition on 42-CrMo steel or a similar transition-metal substrate.
The initial coating has a supersaturated solid-solution matrix and/or coherent nanoprecipitates.
The coating will be tested in sliding wear from 293 K to 1000 K in air at 0.5–2 m/s, 10–50 N, and approximately 100 K temperature increments.
Surface diffusion produces a transient, dense, adherent Cr2O3, Al2O3, or mixed-oxide scale.
From 293–700 K, the oxide scale reduces direct metal-to-metal contact and thereby lowers wear rate.
At low-to-moderate temperature, lattice distortion and coherent precipitates preserve matrix strength.
Above approximately 700–800 K, the oxide scale can become unstable or spall because of thermal-expansion mismatch or phase decomposition.
Above approximately 700–800 K, deformation changes to diffusion-controlled dislocation creep and grain-boundary sliding.
At high temperature, coherent precipitates dissolve or coarsen, causing loss of precipitation strengthening and accelerated plastic deformation.
Wear rate decreases by 30–50% between 293 K and approximately 650 K.
Wear rate increases by a factor of 2–5 above 750 K because of creep-dominated deformation and oxide-scale failure.
Performance degrades near the onset of diffusion-controlled creep, approximated as 0.5 times the alloy melting temperature.
A non-adherent oxide boundary may occur above 800 K in Mn-containing alloys or above 900 K in alloys prone to Laves-phase formation.
The critical temperature depends on composition, oxygen partial pressure, sliding speed, oxide-scale stability, and coating–substrate interdiffusion.

contradictions.description: The proposed degradation threshold shifts among approximately 600–700 K, 700–800 K, above 750 K, above 800 K, above 900 K, and 0.5 Tm without defining which criterion controls the boundary.

The predicted wear-rate curve decreases and then increases, which gives an intermediate minimum or trough, but the falsification rule requires a distinct intermediate-to-high-temperature peak in wear rate.
